Subject: Finalizing SOW + MAP acceptance criteria (tokens/$, caching, batching)

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Marco and I discussed priorities and we want to lock the mutual action plan so procurement can move the SOW through legal. Before we do that we need a short checklist that covers the unit economics assumptions (tokens per call, tokens/$), expected cache hit rates, and batching behavior — basically what your finance + infra teams will validate in the pilot so we can sign.

Can you:
- Confirm the tokens-per-response assumptions for the two main endpoints (summarize & classification)
- Provide recommended batching thresholds and expected latency impacts
- State a conservative caching hit-rate we can use for our forecast (prefetch/prefix cache)

I've attached our draft SOW (NM_MAP_v2_SOW.pdf) and a spreadsheet with our projected traffic. We need the economics doc back by EOD Tuesday (our procurement timeline).

Cheers,
Linda Park
Head of Product, NovaMed

Linda —

Thanks — copying Karthik (solutions) and Neha (finance) for the data. We can get a concise acceptance checklist and a tokens/$ model back by your deadline. High-level notes up front:

- Tokens per call: summary (avg 420 tokens per response, 220 input). classification (avg 120 tokens resp, 80 input). We'll include 10/90 p95 breakdown for longer contexts.
- Batching: recommended max batch window 30ms for low-latency endpoints, 150ms for background classification (saves ~35% token cost at p99 traffic).
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for session resume — expect 18% hit-rate on our conservative baseline for NovaMed's traffic profile; optimistic case 30% with prefetch.

I'll attach a small model (token_cost_model.csv) with our unit calc and a short acceptance checklist; Karthik, can you add the ops-level assumptions (GPU sizing, SLOs) and Neha please flag any finance gating items we should call out in the SOW.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Linda Park <linda@novamed.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco@novamed.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finalizing SOW + MAP acceptance criteria (tokens/$, caching, batching)

Folks —

Quick ops-level writeup that can go into the MAP appendix (copied into the SOW as an exhibit):

1) Token & unit-cost assumptions (conservative):
   - Summary endpoint: input 220 tokens, output 420 tokens -> 640 tokens per call (avg).
   - Classification endpoint: input 80 tokens, output 120 tokens -> 200 tokens per call (avg).
   - Model variant: redwood-medium-1 (quantized) for production MAP; fallback to redwood-small-1 (lower-cost) if latency/backpressure.

2) Batching & latency tradeoffs (recommended defaults for pilot):
   - Low-latency interactive (summary): batch window = 25-40ms, target batch size 1-8 tokens per request (continuous batching enabled). Expected latency p95 + overhead: +18-30ms vs single-request baseline; cost reduction ~12-18% depending on request mix.
   - Bulk classification: batch window = 120-200ms, target batch size 16-64. Expected throughput gains ~2.6x, cost reduction ~30-40%.

3) Caching assumptions: prefix cache + KV cache for session tokens. Conservative baseline: 18% hit-rate (models trained on your traffic pattern). Engineering path to 25-30% via prefetch and client-side hints. Note: cache hit rate is highly workload dependent; include a 10% buffer in your forecast.

4) Unit cost calc example (from attached token_cost_model.csv):
   - redwood-medium-1 token price = $0.00011 per token (hosted, committed pricing assumption).
   - summary avg tokens (640) => $0.0704 per call. With 18% cache hit and 20% batching savings => effective tokens per call ~ 512 => $0.0563 per call.

5) MAP acceptance gates we recommend including in SOW:
   - Cost gate: average token/unit costs within +/-15% of the forecast during 14-day pilot window.
   - Latency gate: p95 <= 450ms for summary endpoint under expected concurrency.
   - Reliability gate: <1% error rate, fallback strategy to smaller model if degraded.

I attached batching_assumptions.xlsx with thresholds and a simple load profile. Happy to jump on a quick call with your infra folks to validate parameter choices.

- Karthik
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: batching_assumptions.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Linda Park <linda@novamed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finalizing SOW + MAP acceptance criteria (tokens/$, caching, batching)

Everyone —

A couple finance clarifications to include in the MAP/SOW before procurement moves:

- Pricing: confirm whether NM-4579 will be on committed capacity (monthly reserved) or on pay-as-you-go hosted. Our unit price example above ($0.00011/token) assumes a 12-month committed profile. If pay-as-you-go, add a 20-30% premium to tokens/$ and re-run the cost model.
- Accounting for cache/batching: recommend a conservative blended forecast line item that assumes only 60% of the projected batching gains during the pilot to avoid underbudgeting.
- Credit/backstop: ask for 10% spend buffer approval in PO for the pilot window to cover traffic shocks.

Also, Jordan — please confirm the fallback model variant and whether we can auto-failover to dedicated capacity if the hosted instance hits SLO limits (we'll capture routing policy in the MAP).

Neha Kapoor
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Subject: MAP checklist & next steps — NM-4579

Linda/Marco —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a one-page MAP acceptance checklist and our revised token_cost_model.csv that incorporates Neha's conservative modifiers (60% batching realization, committed vs PAYG scenarios). Key asks / next steps:

- Please confirm SOW exhibit A (cost gates + acceptance windows) — we marked the cost gate as: pilot average tokens/unit within 15% of forecast, with a 10% spend buffer on the PO.
- Procurement: if you approve, route NM_MAP_v2_SOW.pdf (we added exhibit) to legal/procurement and copy me so I can triage questions.
- Ops sync: Karthik to schedule a 30-min infra deep-dive with your ops team (propose Thu 4/29 10am PT).
- Close timeline: target signature by 5/10 to hit onboarding in June.

If that works I'll update the MAP master and create the canary rollout plan (fallback to redwood-small-1, automatic routing to dedicated if >80% capacity reached for 3m).

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
